terms.definition: The heat energy change measured at constant pressure.
terms.examiner: Standard conditions are 100 kPa and a specified temperature, usually 298 K.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is formed from its elements in their standard states, under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: One mole of the substance; from its elements; standard states. The value for an element in its standard state is zero.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burned completely in oxygen, under standard conditions.
The enthalpy change when one mole of water is formed from an acid and an alkali, under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: Per mole of water formed, not per mole of acid.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change for a reaction is independent of the route taken.
terms.examiner: With formation data: products − reactants. With combustion data: reactants − products.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a bond in the gas phase is broken, averaged over a range of different compounds.
terms.examiner: Values from mean bond enthalpies differ from experimental ones because the real bond enthalpy depends on the molecule, and the data refer to gases.
